script.title: Economic Value Added (EVA) explained simply
script.caption_hook: Profit is not always value. EVA shows why.

lines.say: My company shows profit, but ma'am says it may still destroy value?
That's EVA, Economic Value Added. It is profit after charging for the capital used.
Capital charge? Shareholders' money is already ours, na? Why charge for it?
Equity isn't free. Think of capital as a rented shop. Your earning must first pay the rent.
EVA equals NOPAT minus WACC times capital employed. NOPAT is operating profit after tax, before interest.

board.title: EVA Formula
board.sub: CE = capital employed; WACC = cost of capital

lines.say: Why not deduct interest in NOPAT?
Interest is already inside WACC. Deducting it here too would charge debt twice.
EBIT is ₹10,00,000, tax is 30%. So NOPAT is ₹7,00,000.
Capital employed is ₹50,00,000 and WACC is 12%. Charge is ₹6,00,000. EVA is ₹1,00,000.
Oh! Positive, so value is created!
And if profit is below the charge?
Then EVA is negative. Value is destroyed, even with an accounting profit.
Remember: profit must pay the rent.

check_notes: Writer: Worked example: EBIT ₹10,00,000, tax 30%, NOPAT ₹7,00,000; CE ₹50,00,000 × 12% WACC = ₹6,00,000; EVA ₹1,00,000. WACC given directly. Total about 155 words.

Checker: Line 13 (boy): 'if profit is below the charge' is loose wording. Line 14 then says 'even with an accounting profit', which is profit after interest. Say 'And if NOPAT is below the capital charge?' so the viewer knows which profit is meant.

Checker: Lines 10–11: no period is given for the figures. Say EBIT is ₹10,00,000 per annum and WACC is 12% per annum, so it is clear the EVA of ₹1,00,000 is for one year. The arithmetic is correct: 10,00,000 × 0.70 = 7,00,000; 50,00,000 × 12% = 6,00,000; EVA = 1,00,000.
